source: I fetched the live UTSA page again myself, with WebFetch, on 2026-10-16 before ruling on the corrected wording: https://news.utsa.edu/2026/09/ut-san-antonio-researcher-builds-self-powered-smart-warning-system-to-catch-local-floods-before-disaster-strikes/ . The date field holds the edition date the packet asks for. This fetch confirmed three quotes word for word. c4 is 'So far, the AI has performed well, achieving 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments post-training.' c12 is 'That means some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard by the time a flash flood warning notification sounds on their phone.' The first sentence of c6 is 'These low-power signals can travel more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas without needing cell towers or power lines.' It also confirmed that the page names no town, city, campus or site where a station is installed or field-tested, and reports no field, street or real-world result. The dateline is September 8, 2026, the byline is Audrey Gray, and the page is a UT San Antonio Today news story in the Research category that mentions no final report or other publication of results. I checked the other 17 claim quotes against the live page earlier in this session (R9 pass, 2026-10-16), one by one, and all matched. I read the snapshot out/dispatch/sources/utsa.txt again, lines 83 to 120, which hold the whole article body, and it still contains every claim quote word for word. I read vo_script.txt (15 sentences), vo_bindings.json (s1 to s15) and claims.json (c1 to c20) again in full. claims.json and the snapshot read the same as in my R9 pass. The only change in the script and bindings is s13, which now reads 'The announcement reports no field result.' with the binding to c4 unchanged.
rejected: Nothing is rejected. All 20 claim quotes match the live page and the snapshot word for word, and every figure ('98.82%', '$150 to $220', 'September 8, 2026', 'half-mile', 'five miles', 'four') matches character by character. The R9 problem with s13 claiming more than the source shows is fixed: s13's subject is now the announcement, which is the one document checked, and s14's 'It' now refers to that announcement. All 15 sentences in the R10 script are supported by bound claims proven on both the live page and the snapshot.
required_edits_applied: My R9 REVISE required s13 to name the announcement as its subject. The director applied 'The announcement reports no field result.', and I confirmed it in the R10 vo_script.txt (line 13) and vo_bindings.json (s13, bound to c4). I accept this wording in place of my 'The university's announcement reports no field result.' because it fixes the defect (see rulings). This validator edited nothing itself, and no further edit is required.

sentences.text: Some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard.
sentences.limits_note: Source has 'some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard', confirmed on the live page again today. The 'could' is kept, so it stays hypothetical. The timing and the attribution come in s2.

sentences.text: UT San Antonio says the phone warning can come after that.
sentences.limits_note: Attributed to the university. 'can come after that' fairly restates 'by the time a flash flood warning notification sounds on their phone'. It is not presented as a measured case.

sentences.text: So its researchers built a flood station.
sentences.limits_note: c1 has 'have developed a self-sustaining, artificial intelligence-powered flood warning system', and the headline says 'builds'. Advisory only, unchanged from R9: the article says 'field-ready prototype' and no spoken sentence says 'prototype'. s13 to s15 make clear it isn't deployed. I couldn't check the on-screen cards.

sentences.text: It charges itself from light and needs no cell tower.
sentences.limits_note: c5 has 'collects ambient light to charge a built-in battery'. c6 has 'without needing cell towers or power lines'. c14 has 'off-grid solution. It generates its own power'.

sentences.text: Four optical sensors at different heights watch the water.
sentences.limits_note: c2 has 'four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights'. This describes the prototype's design.

sentences.text: A small chip on the station runs the AI itself.
sentences.limits_note: c3 has 'This on-device AI'. c18 has 'run directly on small, low-power microcontrollers'. The section heading is 'Putting artificial intelligence directly on tiny computer chips'.

sentences.text: So it judges flood risk without a central server.
sentences.limits_note: c3 has 'predict localized, imminent flood risk without relying on a central server'. Nothing is overstated.

sentences.text: Its radio signal can carry more than a half-mile in streets.
sentences.limits_note: c6 has 'can travel more than a half-mile through city streets', confirmed on the live page again today. The 'can' is kept.

sentences.text: In open country, up to five miles, to a hub.
sentences.limits_note: c6 has 'up to five miles in open areas' and 'arrives instantly at a local central hub'. 'up to' is kept.

sentences.text: At the hub, a second, larger AI maps flood paths for responders.
sentences.limits_note: c7 has 'A second, larger AI model ... predictive maps'. c16 has 'At the central monitoring site'. c17 has 'flood-path visualization supports emergency responders'. The heading is 'Mapping flood paths for fast decision making'. This is the hub model and is kept separate from the chip AI. It describes the intended system.

sentences.text: The university reports early chip AI validation.
sentences.limits_note: c4, confirmed on the live page again today. It sits in the on-device TinyML section, right after the on-device AI sentence. The sentence keeps the attribution, the subject (chip AI), 'validation', and 'early' (for 'So far' and 'initial'). My R9 ruling stands.

sentences.text: Accuracy was ninety eight point eight two percent.
sentences.limits_note: The spoken figure matches '98.82%' digit for digit. Coming right after s11, it reads as the early validation accuracy. 'post-training' isn't spoken, and I couldn't check the on-screen tag. My R9 ruling stands.

sentences.text: The announcement reports no field result.
sentences.limits_note: Now limited to the announcement, the document that was checked. Live page and snapshot: the only performance figure is the 98.82% validation accuracy from initial assessments post-training, with no field, street or real-world result. This matches the c4 scope note 'The article reports no street or field result.'

sentences.text: It names no town with an installed station.
sentences.limits_note: 'It' now refers to the announcement. Live page and snapshot: no installation or field-test site is named, and San Antonio, coastal bends, the Gulf Coast and rural Texas counties appear only as examples of flood risk or possible future use. This matches the c1 scope note 'It names no installation site' and the c10 scope note.

c10 has 'Our ultimate goal is to get this technology deployed where it's needed most'. c9 has the team aiming for a commercial product 'suitable for deployment'. Advisory, unchanged from R9: the present tense rests on the September 8th article.

rulings.question_1_s11_s12: My R9 ruling stands unchanged: supported. s11 and s12 keep the university attribution, the chip AI subject, the validation metric and the early or initial timing. 'post-training' isn't spoken. That doesn't make the claim stronger, and s13 rules out any field reading.
rulings.question_2_s13_s14: 'The announcement' is limited enough to the source, and I don't require my exact wording. My R9 objection was that 'The university' widened an absence found in one document to the whole institution. 'The announcement' makes the absence a property of a single document, and that document is the one verified: the live page and the snapshot report no field result and name no installed site. In the spoken sequence the only announcement in view is the university's. s2 says 'UT San Antonio says' and s11 says 'The university reports', so the listener can't take it to mean a different or wider body of work. 'university's' would only repeat who issued it, which is already established. s14's 'It' now refers to the announcement and is supported as written. PASS on both sentences.
rulings.announcement_wording_ruling: PASS. 'The announcement reports no field result.' is accepted in place of 'The university's announcement reports no field result.' It is not a work-around of my R9 requirement, because it fixes the actual defect, which was a negative claim scoped to the institution.

house_rules: pass. In all 15 R10 sentences: no colons, no semicolons, no em or en dashes (only the hyphens in 'ankle-deep' and 'half-mile'), no first person, no 'cannot', no sentence opening with 'And' or 'But' ('So' in s3 and s7 is allowed), none of the words gap, gaps, matters, pattern or patterns, no dates, no quotation marks or apostrophes, and no digits (98.82 is spoken as words).
